title: A sentence
text: mi klama le zarci
gloss: I go to the market.
hint: The stages turn letters into words, then build the sentence.

title: A text with elided terminators
text: lo jbopre cu cusku lu mi klama lo zarci .i do pu tavla mi li'u
gloss: A Lojbanist says: "I go to the market. You talked to me."
hint: Angle brackets such as ⟨ku⟩ and ⟨vau⟩ show terminators that the text omits. Turn off Elided to hide them.

title: An elided terminator comes as late as possible
text: mi tavla lo nanmu poi klama lo zarci
gloss: I talk to a man who goes to the market.
hint: The clause after poi runs to the end of the text. Write ku'o after klama to end the clause there. To see a tie, remove the late step from this directive.

title: An unfinished description
text: mi klama le le
gloss: The text has no complete meaning. It reads "I go to the the" and stops.
hint: The second le starts an inner description, and the text ends before its predicate. The Trace tab shows the parser's progress at the end.

title: Erasing a quoted word with si
text: zo mlatu si zo gerku cu gismu
gloss: The word "gerku" is a root word. The erased words quote the word "mlatu".
hint: A zo quote is one word unit, so si erases zo mlatu as a whole. Open the Tokens tab to compare the stages.

title: Quote an eraser with zo
text: zo si cu cmavo
gloss: The word "si" is a particle.
hint: Here zo quotes si, so it erases nothing.

title: Replacing a phrase with sa
text: mi citka lo badna sa lo plise
gloss: I eat an apple. The erased words say "a banana".
hint: The word sa erases back to the nearest earlier word of the next word's class, here lo.

title: su erases back to an open quote
text: do cusku lu mi klama su mi stali
gloss: You say: "I stay." The erased words say "I go".
hint: su erases the words back to lu, and lu stays. To erase lu too, turn off the feature su-boundary.

title: su erases past an open quote (su-boundary off)
text: do cusku lu mi klama su mi stali
gloss: I stay. The erased words say "You say: I go".
hint: The feature su-boundary is off here, so su erases all the words before it. lojban/zantufa has this feature off by default.

title: Disabling sa-su on an sa text
text: mi citka lo badna sa lo plise
gloss: Intended: I eat an apple. The run stops because the example turns sa-su off.
hint: The words stage turns sa-su on whenever the input has sa or su. Forcing sa-su off in Options produces a feature conflict.

title: lo'u quotes words that make no sentence
text: lo'u mi klama le le le'u na te gerna la lojban
gloss: The words "mi klama le le" are not grammatical text in Lojban.
hint: The words between lo'u and le'u must be Lojban words, but they need no grammar. The quote is one unit.

title: zoi quotes text that is not Lojban
text: mi cusku zoi gy. Hello, world! .gy
gloss: I say "Hello, world!".
hint: The word after zoi is the delimiter. The quote ends where that word comes again.

title: Letter words with bu and compounds with zei
text: .alfa. bu sinxa zoi gy. α .gy. pe lo cmaci zei ciste
gloss: The letter alpha is a symbol for "α" of a mathematical system.
hint: The words stage forms one BY token from .alfa. bu, one ZOI token from zoi, and one BRIVLA from zei.

title: Lojban written in Cyrillic
text: ми клама ле зарши
gloss: I go to the market.
hint: The phonemes stage maps Cyrillic letters to Lojban sounds, so syntax reads mi klama le zarci. With cll-cyrillic off, lojban/cll reads no Cyrillic.

lojban/bpfk.hint: The phonemes stage maps Cyrillic letters to Lojban sounds, so syntax reads mi klama le zarci. The text шои до reads as co'i do, and as coi do with cll-cyrillic on.

lojban/experimental.hint: The phonemes stage maps Cyrillic letters to Lojban sounds, so syntax reads mi klama le zarci. The text шои до reads as co'i do, and as coi do with cll-cyrillic on.

lojban/zantufa.hint: The phonemes stage maps Cyrillic letters to Lojban sounds, so syntax reads mi klama le zarci. The text шои до reads as co'i do, and as coi do with cll-cyrillic on.

title: Attach a feeling to a sentence
text: .ui mi viska do
gloss: I am happy that I see you.
hint: The initial ui expresses the speaker's feeling.

title: Write a number with a digit
text: mi ponse 2 gerku
gloss: I own two dogs.
hint: The phonemes stage reads 2 as re. Compare this with the CLL pipeline.

title: CLL requires a spelled number
text: mi ponse 2 gerku
gloss: Intended: I own two dogs.
hint: CLL treats 2 as foreign text. Replace it with re to say "I own two dogs."

title: An extended rafsi on a borrowing
text: lo cidja cu spageti'ykukte
gloss: The food is spaghetti-delicious. The compound joins the words for spaghetti and for delicious.
hint: Extended rafsi rules join the borrowing spageti to kukte with 'y as one compound word. Switch to lojban/cll to see CLL 1.1 reject this form.

title: CLL has no extended rafsi
text: lo cidja cu spageti'ykukte
gloss: Intended: The food is spaghetti-delicious.
hint: CLL 1.1 has no extended rafsi, so the words stage cannot read this compound. Write spageti zei kukte to join the two words.

title: The earliest, longest tense wins
text: mi viska pu va ca gi do gi la djan
gloss: Earlier and some distance away, I saw you at the same time as John.
hint: The stage prefers the earliest and longest simple-tense-modal group, so pu va wins. Remove the leftmost-longest step from the pipeline directive to see a tie.

title: A ranked choice in connectives
text: lo kosta cu blabi joi ke xekri blanu ke'e
gloss: The coat is white mixed with dark blue.
hint: The ranked choice ≻ gives ke to the joi connective rather than the right tanru unit. Replace ≻ with | in afterthought-connection to see a tie.

title: A name word used as a predicate
text: lo mlatu pe mi cu .feliks.
gloss: My cat is Felix.
hint: With cbm on, a cmevla can act directly as a predicate. Set cbm to Off in Options to reject .feliks. after cu.

lojban/zantufa.hint: Zantufa always allows a cmevla as a predicate. Switch to lojban/experimental to toggle this form with the cbm feature.

title: Turn the name feature off
text: lo mlatu pe mi cu .feliks.
gloss: Intended: My cat is Felix.
hint: The same name cannot act as a predicate with cbm off. Turn cbm on to accept this experimental form.

title: A consonant-glide name and its warning
text: la .tokios. cu barda tcadu
gloss: Tokyo is a big city.
hint: Experimental accepts the consonant-glide onset kio in .tokios. with a warning. Switch to lojban/bpfk to reject it, or to lojban/cll to accept it without warning.

title: Closing a name phrase before a predicate
text: mi klama lo zarci sei la .alis. cusku
gloss: I go to the market, Alice says.
hint: Unlike a PEG parser, gencmu does not commit greedily to la .alis. cusku as one description, so cusku remains the sei predicate.

title: A condition on me arguments
text: lo vi karda cu me by
gloss: This card is among B. Here B names a group of cards.
hint: Let B name a group of cards. This card belongs to that group. The condition prefers the argument reading of by. Remove the %conditions clause from me-unit to see a tie.

lojban/zantufa.hint: Let B name a group of cards. This card belongs to that group. The condition prefers the argument reading of by. Remove the line ¬$m.without-elision.parse(sumti), from tanru-unit-1 to see a tie.

title: Discourse frames with ki'ei
text: ki'ei pu zu ku .i lo nolraitru cu xabju lo galtu dinju .i ro prenu cu tirna ko'a ki'ei ca ku .i lo dinju cu spofu
gloss: Long ago: the king lived in a high building, and everyone heard him. Now: the building is broken. The text does not say who "him" is. The gloss reads him as the king.
hint: The first frame puts two sentences in the distant past. The second frame returns to the present. This example pipeline includes lojban/cll and adds ki'ei frames in one short document. Switch to lojban/cll to see plain CLL reject ki'ei.
